title: Applied anatomy: the abdominal aorta and its branches

brief.scenario: This is a verbal applied anatomy viva on the abdominal aorta. The examiner will read out descriptions of a dissection of the posterior abdominal wall and of a contrast CT angiogram of the abdomen, and ask you to name the vessels described.
brief.task: Name the vessels from the examiner's descriptions and answer questions on the aorta's branches and their surgical relevance.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Three unpaired anterior branches at three levels, then the relations that matter at surgery.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Forgetting the left renal vein, which crosses in front of the aorta just below the SMA.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Start from the top: "The aorta enters through the aortic hiatus at T12."

grid.label: Unpaired branches and levels
grid.fail: Gives the wrong order or levels of the unpaired branches.
grid.borderline: Gets the order right but places each level a vertebra out.
grid.pass: Coeliac T12, superior mesenteric L1, inferior mesenteric L3; bifurcation L4.
grid.high: Adds entry through the aortic hiatus at T12, and that the bifurcation lies at the level of the iliac crests.

grid.label: Coeliac trunk
grid.fail: Includes the superior mesenteric artery as a coeliac branch.
grid.pass: Left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries.
grid.high: Follows the branches, e.g. gastroduodenal from the common hepatic: the vessel eroded by a posterior duodenal ulcer.

grid.label: Superior mesenteric artery relations
grid.pass: Passes behind the neck of the pancreas, in front of the uncinate process and third part of the duodenum.
grid.high: Explains the left renal vein running between aorta and SMA, and how a narrow angle can compress it or the duodenum.

grid.label: Paired branches
grid.fail: Omits the renal arteries, or places them above the coeliac trunk.
grid.pass: Suprarenal, renal and gonadal arteries; renal arteries at about L1–L2.
grid.high: Adds that the right renal artery passes behind the IVC, and the longer left renal vein crosses in front of the aorta.

grid.label: Inferior mesenteric artery and collaterals
grid.pass: Left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal arteries; the marginal artery links IMA and SMA territories.
grid.high: Names the watershed areas at the splenic flexure and rectosigmoid, and links IMA ligation in aortic surgery to sigmoid ischaemia.

grid.label: Aneurysm thresholds
grid.fail: Gives a repair threshold without a size, or the wrong size.
grid.pass: Consider repair if symptomatic, if 5.5 cm or larger, or if over 4.0 cm and grown more than 1 cm in a year.
grid.high: Adds referral: seen by the regional vascular service within 2 weeks at 5.5 cm or larger, within 12 weeks at 3.0–5.4 cm.

grid.label: Relations at aneurysm surgery
grid.fail: Doesn't know where the renal arteries lie relative to a typical aneurysm.
grid.pass: Most aneurysms are infrarenal: the neck lies below the renal arteries, with the left renal vein across it.
grid.high: Explains why the length of the infrarenal neck matters for endovascular repair, and that the left renal vein is at risk when clamping.

grid.label: Handling uncertainty
grid.fail: Names a vessel confidently and wrongly when unsure.
grid.pass: States uncertainty, then reasons from the described origin and course before naming.
grid.high: Gives a two-item differential with a reason, then commits.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Give me the unpaired branches and their levels.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The SMA first, then the coeliac trunk, then the IMA.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Left gastric, splenic, and the superior mesenteric.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What lies between the SMA and the aorta?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: When would you repair an aneurysm?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: On the sagittal CT angiogram, a second vessel arises from the front of the aorta just below that trunk and runs downwards and forwards behind the neck of the pancreas. What is it?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That's definitely the inferior mesenteric artery.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Give me the unpaired branches and their levels.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Coeliac trunk at T12, superior mesenteric at L1, inferior mesenteric at L3. The aorta bifurcates at L4.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Left gastric, splenic and common hepatic.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It passes behind the neck of the pancreas, then in front of the uncinate process and the third part of the duodenum.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Suprarenal, renal and gonadal. The renal arteries arise at about L1 to L2.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal branches. The marginal artery connects it with the SMA territory.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: When would you consider repairing an aneurysm?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: If it's symptomatic, if it's 5.5 cm or larger, or if it's over 4 cm and has grown more than 1 cm in a year.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Where does a typical aneurysm sit?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Below the renal arteries. The left renal vein crosses the neck anteriorly.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: On the sagittal CT angiogram, a second vessel arises from the front of the aorta just below that trunk and runs downwards and forwards behind the neck of the pancreas. What is it?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'm not certain. It arises from the front of the aorta just below the coeliac trunk and runs behind the pancreas, so I think it's the SMA.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Give me the unpaired branches and their levels.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The aorta enters through the aortic hiatus at T12. Coeliac trunk at T12, superior mesenteric at L1, inferior mesenteric at L3, bifurcating at L4, roughly the level of the iliac crests.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Left gastric, splenic and common hepatic. The common hepatic gives the gastroduodenal, which is the vessel a posterior duodenal ulcer erodes.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Behind the pancreatic neck, in front of the uncinate process and third part of the duodenum. The left renal vein runs between the SMA and the aorta, so a narrow angle can compress the vein or the duodenum.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Suprarenal, renal and gonadal. The right renal artery passes behind the IVC; the left renal vein is longer and crosses in front of the aorta.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Left colic, sigmoid and superior rectal. The marginal artery joins it to the SMA, with watershed areas at the splenic flexure and rectosigmoid, which is why IMA ligation during aortic repair can cause sigmoid ischaemia.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Consider repair if symptomatic, at 5.5 cm or larger, or over 4 cm with more than 1 cm growth in a year. At 5.5 cm or more they should be seen by the regional vascular service within 2 weeks; at 3.0 to 5.4 cm, within 12 weeks.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Most are infrarenal, so the length of the neck below the renal arteries decides whether endovascular repair is feasible. The left renal vein lies across the neck and is at risk when clamping.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: On the sagittal CT angiogram, a second vessel arises from the front of the aorta just below that trunk and runs downwards and forwards behind the neck of the pancreas. What is it?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's either the SMA or the coeliac trunk. It arises below the trunk's three branches and passes behind the pancreatic neck, so it's the SMA.

failures.move: Placing the renal arteries above the coeliac trunk.
failures.consequence: Breaks the level sequence the rest of the station relies on.

failures.move: Not knowing the IMA's collateral supply.
failures.consequence: Cannot explain colonic ischaemia after aortic surgery.

failures.move: Forgetting the left renal vein across the aneurysm neck.
failures.consequence: Misses the structure most at risk during clamping.
A threshold without a number is not a threshold.

recovery.line: I can't name that with certainty. From its origin and course, I'd favour X over Y, because…
Let me anchor it: the aorta enters at T12 and bifurcates at L4, and the three unpaired branches sit between.

knowledge.fact: Levels: coeliac T12, SMA L1, renals about L1–L2, IMA L3, bifurcation L4.
The left renal vein crosses anterior to the aorta, just below the SMA.
Consider repair: symptomatic; 5.5 cm or larger; or over 4.0 cm with more than 1 cm growth in 1 year.
Refer to the regional vascular service: seen within 2 weeks at 5.5 cm or larger; within 12 weeks at 3.0–5.4 cm.
Surveillance: yearly at 3.0–4.4 cm; 3-monthly at 4.5–5.4 cm.

recall.think: Which level, which relation, and what is at risk at surgery?
recall.say: "Coeliac T12, SMA L1, IMA L3, bifurcation L4."
do: Anchor the levels from the hiatus down
Name the left renal vein's relation
recall.trap: Forgetting the left renal vein across the neck.
recall.finish: Symptomatic or ≥ 5.5 cm: regional vascular service within 2 weeks.

partner.opening: This is a verbal viva on the abdominal aorta. I'll describe a dissection of the posterior abdominal wall and a CT angiogram. Start with the aorta and give me its branches in order.

reveals.finding: Read out: in the dissection, a short, wide trunk arises from the front of the aorta just below the diaphragm and divides almost at once into three branches: one passing upwards and to the left towards the stomach, one running to the left along the upper border of the pancreas, and one running to the right. Ask what the trunk and its three branches are.
Read out: on the sagittal CT angiogram, a second vessel arises from the front of the aorta just below that trunk and runs downwards and forwards behind the neck of the pancreas. Ask what it is.

Read out: on an axial CT slice just below the origin of that vessel, a vein passes from left to right between it and the front of the aorta to join the inferior vena cava. Ask what the vein is and why it matters.

push.question: What are the paired branches, and where do the renal arteries arise?
push.expect: Suprarenal, renal, gonadal; renals about L1–L2; right renal artery behind the IVC.

push.question: What are the IMA's branches, and why does it matter in aortic surgery?
push.expect: Left colic, sigmoid, superior rectal; marginal artery; watershed areas; sigmoid ischaemia.

push.question: When would you consider repairing an asymptomatic aneurysm?
push.expect: 5.5 cm or larger, or over 4.0 cm with more than 1 cm growth in a year.

push.question: What decides whether endovascular repair is possible?
push.expect: Length of the infrarenal neck below the renal arteries.

curveballs.prompt: His aneurysm is 4.8 cm and he's now tender over it. What do you do?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Symptomatic aneurysm: consider repair regardless of size and involve the vascular team now.

curveballs.prompt: After aortic repair he passes bloody diarrhoea. Why?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Possible sigmoid ischaemia from IMA ligation with poor collateral supply.

curveballs.prompt: What runs between the SMA and the aorta?
curveballs.safeAnswer: The left renal vein, and below it the third part of the duodenum.
